headline: Recommended approval, as amended, of zoning changes on accessory dwelling units and removing ground story elevation requirements.
summary: Councilors debated whether to add stricter local limits on accessory dwelling units (ADUs), and Councilor McLaughlin opposed further limits. The committee said there is no immediate deadline, because state rules are still being clarified. The committee also approved revised text for the ground story elevation change.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Land Use Committee Meeting Minutes

Thursday, November 19, 2026

6:30 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Ewen-Campen at 6:32pm and adjourned at 7:17pm on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Davis, Clingan, Sait, McLaughlin, Ewen-Campen) and 0 absent.

Others present: Dan Bartman - Director of Strategy and Development, Madalyn Letellier - Assistant City Clerk, Legislative Services.

Roll Call

- Present: Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis, Ward Four City
- Councilor Jesse Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Naima
- Sait, Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin and
- Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Land Use Committee Meeting of October

Minutes

29, 2026.

(ID # 26-1665 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- Ward Six City Councilor Davis, Ward Four City Councilor
- Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait, Ward One City
- Councilor McLaughlin and Ward Three City Councilor
- Ewen-Campen

2. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Land Use Committee Meeting of November

Minutes

5, 2026.

(ID # 26-1666 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- Ward Six City Councilor Davis, Ward Four City Councilor
- Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait, Ward One City
- Councilor McLaughlin and Ward Three City Councilor
- Ewen-Campen

3. Mayor's Request Requesting ordainment of an amendment to Sections 3.1.3, 3.1.6, 3.1.8, (ID # 26-1336 ) 3.1.9, 3.1.11, 3.1.12, 3.1.13, 3.1.16, 3.2.6 of the Somerville Zoning

- Ordinance to align with State Law regarding protected accessory dwelling
- units.

Councilor Davis read a public comment submitted by Senator Jehlen into

the record (Land Use - 2026-11-19 Public Comment (with 26-1336 ),

highlighting that the second half of the correspondence aligns with councilor concerns that proposed local regulations conflict with state law, and asked the committee to consider if further amendments should be explored before

approving. Chair Ewen-Campen recapped prior discussions, noting that while state regulations exist, builders may choose to follow state law

directly, leaving the city potentially unable to enforce stricter local proposals. Director Bartman clarified that state statute empowers the Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC) to establish its own regulations and added that because the community is

already out of compliance, developers are unlikely to leverage state law against more restrictive local zoning. Councilor McLaughlin spoke against

further amendments that would restrict accessory dwelling units (ADUs), referencing a map of existing ADUs (Land Use - 2026-11-19 Map (with

26-1259) and noting that the city originally voted to permit them. Councilor

- Davis stated that massing, gross floor area, story height, and recent tree
- provision amendments should capture the committee's intended goals.

- Following remarks from Councilor Sait, the committee discussed that there

is no immediate time crunch as state legislation is actively working to clarify the regulations and noted that the proposed amendment provides an

attractive local zoning option as an alternative pathway to state zoning for building compliant ADUs. Councilors also spoke to the importance to tree

preservation in the city and there are penalties in place if someone were to break state or city ordinances, Chair Ewen-Campen highlighted while that is an important subject it is not pertinent to the conversation at hand.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AS

AMENDED

AYE:

- Ward Six City Councilor Davis, Ward Four City Councilor
- Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait, Ward One City
- Councilor McLaughlin and Ward Three City Councilor
- Ewen-Campen

4. Mayor's Request Requesting ordainment of an amendment to Sections 2.4.4, 3.1.7, 3.1.8, (ID # 26-1259 ) 3.1.9, 3.1.10, 3.1.11, 3.2.7, 3.2.8, 3.2.9, 3.2.10, 3.2.11, 4.1.7, 4.2.7, 4.3.7, 4.4.7 of the Somerville Zoning Ordinances to remove ground story elevation

- requirements.

Chair Ewen-Campen explained the item was sent back to committee to accommodate extra amendments that were made by the City Council Land

- Use Analyst following discussion in committee.

Chair Ewen-Campen moved to replace the document PADU

Compliance Amendment 09.08.2026 attached to item #26-1259 with the document Land Use - 2026-11-19 Ground Story Elevation Raised

Amendment (with 26-1259) attached to tonight’s agenda. The motion

was approved on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Davis, Clingan, Sait, McLaughlin, Ewen-Campen).

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AS

AMENDED

AYE:

- Ward Six City Councilor Davis, Ward Four City Councilor
- Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait, Ward One City
- Councilor McLaughlin and Ward Three City Councilor
- Ewen-Campen
